messages:
emma_oncall: Heads up, we had a night of repeat DB-connection pages (02:08-02:52 UTC). Looks like a recurring pattern the last 3 nights. Postmortem stub: https://redwood.internal/ops/pm-db-spike-2245. Need owners for tuning + recurrence tracking.

raj.engineer: digging in. early read: cron batch plus transient connection flaps. Alert is `DBConnErrorRate > 0.02 for 2m` and is scoped by `instance`, so we get multiple pages when multiple instances hit it briefly.

leo_sre: can you paste the alert rule (sanitized)? want to see grouping/labels and eval_interval.

raj.engineer: rule (sanitized):
```yaml
alert: DBConnectionErrorsHigh
expr: sum by(instance)(increase(db_connection_errors_total[2m])) / sum by(instance)(increase(db_connection_attempts_total[2m])) > 0.02
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
  team: storage
```
We have eval_interval = 1m.

leo_sre: two obvious levers: 1) change cardinality (sum by service instead of instance) so duplicates collapse; 2) increase evaluation window to 5m or use for: 5m so brief spikes don't page. Also consider a hysteresis: severity -> warn then page if sustained.

maya_pm: timeline question: we need a quick mitigation to stop customer noise and a medium plan to avoid missing real regressions. Also want tracking of "recurring incident" tags so we can report weekly.

emma_oncall: Quick mitigation idea: change rule to `sum by(service)` and bump `for` to 5m in staging, run synthetic job that simulates cron spike. If staging looks good, prod deploy with a 24h monitoring window. I'll own rollout.

raj.engineer: medium plan: add a two-tier alert (warning at 1m+threshold, page at 5m+higher threshold) and add a suppression rule in Alertmanager that rate-limits pages per service (max 1 page per 15m unless severity increases). Will draft PRs.

leo_sre: For recurrence tracking we should tag incident tickets with `recurring:true` and increment a metric `incidents.recurring.count{alert=DBConnectionErrorsHigh}` so we can graph weekly. I'll add that to the runbook.

alerts-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2245-db-conn-noise. Owners assigned: emma_oncall (rollout), raj.engineer (alert rule changes), leo_sre (runbook + recurrence metric). Due: 2024-06-10.

maya_pm: Action items recap:
- emma_oncall: staging change (sum by service + for=5m) + smoke test (due 2024-06-05)
- raj.engineer: PR for two-tier thresholds + Alertmanager rate-limit policy (due 2024-06-12)
- leo_sre: runbook update + recurring incident metric + dashboard (due 2024-06-17)
- maya_pm: customer comms & weekly recurrence report setup (due 2024-06-14)

emma_oncall: Smoke test plan: create synthetic job that emits connection errors on 3 instances simultaneously for 90s then stop; acceptance: single page (service-level) or only a WARN, no >3 pages in 10m. Rollback: revert rule and redeploy.

raj.engineer: important safety note: ensure we don't mask real multi-instance failures (e.g., full cluster outage). Playbook must include an increased-severity path: if total error rate across service > 10% then immediate page to oncall regardless of suppression.

leo_sre: Agree. I'll add an automatic escalation rule that ignores rate-limits when a separate "service-wide" metric crosses a critical threshold. Also will add an alert fingerprinting note: compute fingerprint using service+cluster only.

maya_pm: Let's aim to reduce duplicate pages by >=95% for this alert without increasing time-to-detect for true incidents. We'll measure with `pages.alert.DBConnectionErrorsHigh` delta week-over-week.

emma_oncall: Scheduling a 20m sync tomorrow 09:30 UTC to walk through smoke steps and acceptance criteria. Please update the incident ticket with any subtasks.

raj.engineer: I'll open the PRs after the staging smoke passes and tag reviewers.

leo_sre: I'll also add a short postmortem checklist entry: "If recurring pattern >2x/week, escalate to infra reliability team for deeper analysis".

alerts-bot: Follow-up reminder set for 2024-06-18 08:00 UTC.

maya_pm: thanks all — if anyone needs to swap tasks ping me. I'll draft the customer note once emma confirms staging results. :memo:
